o.text: From Classical Persian کِلِید (kilīd), from Middle Persian *kilēd, from Ancient Greek κλείς (kleís), from Proto-Hellenic *klāwī́ds, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u-.

A derivation of Proto-Turkic *kay- (“to turn back”), whence also Azerbaijani qayıtmaq (“to come back”). Cognate with Karakhanid قَیْتَرْماق (qaytarmāq, “turn back”), which Kashgari reported to be an Oghuz word, Kipchak qaytar- (“to return something”).
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish دویمك (döymek), دوزمك (dözmek), from Proto-Turkic *töŕ-, whence also Hungarian tűr (“to endure, tolerate”).
From əl + veriş + -li. Compare Turkish elverişli.
Present participle compound of işə (“work”) (dative) + götür- (“to take”).
